adds.title: IDEMPOTENCE_CONFLATED_WITH_DETERMINISM
adds.evidence: T1-B says that if f(f(x)) != f(x), matching becomes no determinista entre corridas.
adds.impact: Learner may conflate two different guarantees: determinism means same input gives same output; idempotence means reapplying the transformation does not change the result.
adds.attack: A function such as f(x)=x+1 is deterministic and not idempotent. The S28 risk is repeated transformation/drift across stages, not randomness.
adds.defense: The paragraph is trying to explain an operational symptom of repeated normalization rather than formally define determinism.
